prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / environment composition edit.
Input 1 is the existing 1080 x 2400, 9:20 mobile rocky ground background. Input 2 is a STRICT LINE AND CEL-SHADING STYLE REFERENCE from the same game. Do not copy the gate from input 2.
Make THREE requested changes: (1) MUCH THICKER dark plum outlines matching the game's chunky icons, (2) scatter the few stone and root accents farther apart, not a little central pile, and (3) turn the tiny puddle into a genuinely LARGE LAKE as part of the environment.
STYLE: All outlined stones, moss, roots and the lake shore have clean confident very thick deep-plum contours, around 18–22 pixels thick at 1080 output width, rounded joins, smooth bold silhouettes, and 2–3 broad flat cel-shaded color regions. The lines must be visibly heavier than input 1. No thin sketch lines, gritty detail, realistic texture, gradients inside objects or intricate highlights. Preserve the pale warm-gray / taupe / muted lavender ground palette and the original quiet ground patch scale; only the accents have strong outlines.
LAYOUT: Keep the entire upper 0–54% primarily clear rocky ground so the game board can cover it. Preserve a modest cropped left-edge flat rocky ledge around the upper-middle, restyled with the bolder contour. Remove the old tight cluster under the board and recompose the accents over a broader area. Put the small mossy flat stone on dry ground toward the LOWER LEFT, centered around 24% width and 61% height, about 16% of canvas width. Put the short brown root well away from it, on dry ground toward the RIGHT around 77% width and 57% height, about 15% of canvas width, rotated on a different diagonal. Leave generous empty floor between them, about three stone widths. Scatter only a few unequal tiny pebbles with irregular offsets; no vertical rows, mirrored placements, evenly spaced dots or repeat clusters. The stone and root should still fall in the exposed band below the board and above the creature tray on tall phones.
LAKE: Replace the tiny self-contained puddle entirely. Draw a LARGE muted blue-gray lake occupying the LOWER-RIGHT portion of the world, with water continuing OFF BOTH the right edge and bottom edge of the canvas. It must clearly read as a large body of water extending beyond the screen, not another floating puddle icon. The upper shoreline starts in the lower-middle around 55–65% of canvas width and 62–64% height, then meanders naturally outward, with the lake widening toward the bottom-right. By the bottom quarter, water occupies roughly the right half of the canvas. Keep the upper visible shoreline and blue water reaching into the middle third of the width so they survive mobile crops. Use a bold irregular dark-plum shore outline and a restrained narrow pale stone bank, two simple blue-gray water tones, and only one or two broad gentle reflection/ripple marks. No photorealistic waves, tiny ripples, sparkles, islands, fish, boats or props. The lake must remain below the board area and should not touch or visually merge with the separate root or mossy stone. No objects are lined up along its shore.
The scene is strictly an OVERHEAD view of continuous flat ground and a lake, not a side-view landscape: no horizon, cave walls, cliffs or perspective. No board, grid lines, purple divider, border around the whole image, UI, text or creatures. Opaque full bleed 1080 x 2400 portrait. Output only the revised background.
refinement_prompt: Precise localized edit to this exact 1080 x 2400 (9:20) rocky lake background. Keep the entire lake, bold shoreline, mossy stones, left ledge, scattered pebbles, colors and ground pattern unchanged. Move ONLY the brown root: remove it from its present upper-right position and put it on the empty DRY GROUND toward the LOWER LEFT of the visible lake shore, centered about 37% of canvas width and 70% of canvas height. Keep its current size (roughly 20–22% of canvas width), thick dark plum outline and simple flat cel shading, but rotate it slightly so it runs diagonally down to the right. The root must be entirely on pale dry land, separated from the lake outline by an obvious small gap, not floating on or crossing the water. It must be clearly separated from the mossy stone above-left; do not form a tight pile. Its whole bounding box should be within approximately x=25–49% of width and y=66–73% of height, keeping it below the board and above the creature tray on tall phones. Restore matching quiet ground at the old position. Change nothing else. Preserve the very bold 18–22px dark-plum line style, the broad lake extending off the bottom and right edges, and the quiet upper half. Output only the finished background.
